label: DUPLICATE-of-E12
headline: Meridia Traffic Rebounds to 53 Vessels Daily as Convoys Resume
body: QOROS — Global shipping flows through the Strait of Meridia have resumed at a fraction of normal capacity, with HarborTrack recording 53 transits on 20 September against a pre-crisis norm of 140 ships per day. The uptick coincides with the inaugural Operation Open Water convoys, sanctioned by the Meridian Compact and escorted by navies from Khoreth, Sundaria, Elbar, Aldenport, and Virelles. Qoros Marine Underwriters' Association reports the Meridia Route Normalization Index has climbed to 38, reflecting a partial easing of war-risk premiums but far from the 100-point baseline required for full market recovery. "We are seeing a disciplined return of dry-bulk and container traffic, but only within the escorted windows," said a senior broker at a Qoros firm. "Freight rates remain elevated, but the certainty of passage is stabilizing the market." Varessan Coastal Forces monitored the transit zone without engagement, though tension persists near the outer limits of the channel. Shippers note that while the 38 percent utilization rate provides critical relief, full normalization depends on sustained security guarantees. The Meridian Compact has urged further integration of commercial routing data to optimize convoy schedules.
